full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Karim, J.: This first Miscellaneous appeal at the instance of defendant No. 2 Khawja Habibullah Askari is directed against order dated 17.6.1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 6 of 1997 refusing the prayer of the defendant for temporary injunction for restraining plaintiff no.1 Khawja Zaki Ahsanullah from entering into the premises of Nawab Askari Jute Mills Limited or interfering with the management of the mills by defendant no. 2 till disposal of the suit. 

 2. This first miscellaneous appeal arises out of Title Suit No. 6 of 1997 filed by plaintiff no. 1 respondent no. 1 Khawja Zaki Ahsanullah stating, inter alia, that plaintiff no. 2 Nawab Askari Jute Mills Limited is a company incorporated in 1968 under the companies Act, 1913, for the purpose of manufacturing finished jute products with 40% of its shareholding held by Khawja Alimilla Walsh. Estate (hereinafter referred to as the Wakfa State) and 40% to be sold to the general public and remaining 20% being held by East Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation. The process for selling of the shares to the public was completed in 1970-71, but the actual sale could not take place owning to the prevailing political situation of that period. Nationalised in 1972, the mills were denationalised and handed over to the Wakf Estate on 31.7.1985. Under the Articles of Association, the Board of Directors could elect its chairman and also the Managing Director, plaintiff No. 1 was appointed the Mutawalli of the wakf Estate by wakf Administrator, but his appointment was cancelled on 10.1.1985 by the Administrator of wakf as per direction of the Chief Martial Law Administrator and defen-dant No. 1 Khawja Abdul Gani was appointed official Mutawalli on 28.1.1985 and a 8 member administrative committee was formed for the administration of the wakf Estate. Being aggrieved by the order dated 28.1.1985, plaintiff no. 1 filed writ petition No. 119 of 1985 and defendant no. 2 Khawja Habibullah Askari filed Writ Petition no 246 of 1985 and a Division Bench court cancelled the appointment of the earlier official Mutawalli appointed by the Wakf administrator with a direction to him to constitute a Managing Committee of eight with the eight members a Managing Committee of eight with the eight members as mentioned in the order dated 28.1.1985 with a further direction that the defendant no. 1 Nawabzada Khawja Abdul Gani will act as the convener of the committee, which would function on the decision of the majority members. It is further stated in the plaint that in 1992 the said management commit-tee nominated plaintiff no. 1 as director to the Board of Directors of plaintiff no. 2 company and, in its first Board Meeting, plain-tiff no. 2 company and, in its first Board Meeting, plaintiff no. 1 was elected Managing Director of the company for a period of three years and in 1995 he was re-elected the Managing Director by the Board of another term of three years. It is further mentioned that on 2.4.1996 plaintiff no. 1 having obtained leave from the Board, went abroad for family reasons and on his return on 4.7.1996, continued to act as the Managing Director and duly conducted the Board had empowered the secretary of plaintiff no. 2 Company to run the day-to-day affairs of the Company as its acting Managing Director. It is further averred in the plaint the on 10.5.1996 while plaintiff no. 1. was on leave, defendant no. 2 forcibly entered into the premises of the Company causing loss and damage to the assets and documents of the office for which the acting Managing Director lodged a first information report on 25.5.1996 with police station Motijheel and a warrant was issued against defendant no. 2, who is on bail now. It is further stated that on 19.5.1996 while plaintiff no. 1 was on leave. Defendant no. 2 called a meeting of the Wakf Estate Managing Committee and by a letter dated 14.5.1996 the members of the committee were informed of its decision about cancellation of the appointment of plaintiff no. 1 as the Managing Director of the Company and the appointment of defendant no. 2 as the Managing director in his place. It is claimed that the said decision of the Wakf Estate management committee is arbitrary, illegal and taken in clear violation of the Articles of Association of the Company. The suit was filed for a declaration that plaintiff no. 1 is Managing Director of the Company with a prayer for permanent injunction restraining defendant no. 2 Khawja Habibullah Askari from interfering with the management of the company. 

 7. The Managing Committee of the Wakf Estate in its meeting held on 14.5.1996 proposed to appoint defendant no. 2 appellant Nawab Khawja Habibullah Askari Managing Director of the Company in place of plaintiff-respondent no.1 Khawja Zaki Ahsanullah on the ground of causing ruination of the assets of the Jute Mills. The proposal of appointing defendant no. 2 appellant Managing Director in place of plaintiff-respondent no. 1 is said to have been endorsed by the Board of Directors of the Company in its meeting held on 11.9.1996. A copy of the minutes of the said meeting said to have been held on 11.9.1996 shows the election of defendant no. 2 appellant as the Managing Director in place of plaintiff-respondent no. 1 by endorsing the decision of the Managing Committee of the Wakf State. It is submitted by Mr. BazIur Rahman Talukder that the proceedings of the wakf Estate Managing Committee of 14.5.1996 and of the Board of Directors of 11.9.1996 about election of defendant no. 2 appellant as Managing Director go a long way to show the re-election of plaintiff respondent no. 1 as Managing Director for another term of three years after the expiry of the first term on 23.2.1995. We do not make any comment on this submission, because it is for the trial court to frame issues and decide the case in accordance with law. 

 12. Before concluding, we may mention that on their application, the court Wards, Dhaka Nawab Estate, was added as a respondent. The trial court should decide if the court of wards should be added a party to the suit, if any application is filed by them.
